extracted.intended_audience: Entities applying to or participating in the FCC Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program and the Enhanced Competition Incentive Program (ECIP) — e.g., providers of advanced communications service, licensees, assignees, lessees, small carriers, and Tribal Nations.
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and programmatic criteria for (1) the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program (funding, claims, disposal, reporting, audits, enforcement, Replacement List and reporting obligations) and (2) the Enhanced Competition Incentive Program (ECIP) application, eligibility, benefits, obligations, construction/operational requirements, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro-rata reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: When pro-rata reductions are required, the Wireline Competition Bureau shall: (i) divide the total remaining funds available by the demand within the specific prioritization category to produce a pro-rata factor; (ii) multiply the pro-rata factor by the total dollar amount requested by each recipient in the prioritization category; and (iii) allocate funds to each recipient consistent with this calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement claim shows actual expenses reasonably incurred
rubrics_metrics.description: A Reimbursement Program recipient must show in the reimbursement claim actual expenses reasonably incurred for the removal, replacement, and disposal of covered communications equipment or service; the Wireline Competition Bureau will review and grant or deny reimbursement claims for actual costs reasonably incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial reimbursement claim filing within one year
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year of approval of its Reimbursement Program application, a recipient must file at least one reimbursement claim; failure to file within one year results in reclamation of all allocated funding and reversion to the Program fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement claim deadline (120 days after term expiration)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reimbursement claims must be filed by the recipient within 120 days of expiration of the removal, replacement and disposal term; after the reimbursement claim deadline any remaining and unclaimed funding allocated to the recipient will automatically be reclaimed and revert to the Program fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of reimbursement claim deadline (one extension, ≤120 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may request a single extension of the reimbursement claim deadline by no later than the deadline; the Wireline Competition Bureau shall grant any timely filed extension request for no more than 120 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal, replacement, and disposal term (one-year completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must complete the permanent removal, replacement, and disposal of covered communications equipment or service within one year of receiving the initial draw down disbursement from their funding allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General six-month extension for all recipients (supply inadequacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may extend by six months the removal/replacement/disposal term to all recipients if it finds the supply of replacement communications equipment or services is inadequate to meet recipients' needs and provides notice and detailed justification to specified congressional committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be provided to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual extension for no-fault inability (up to six months, possibly multiple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to term expiration a recipient may petition the Wireline Competition Bureau for an extension; the Bureau may grant up to six months after finding that, due to no fault of the recipient, the recipient is unable to complete permanent removal, replacement, and disposal by the end of the term. More than one extension may be granted if circumstances warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on funding use — timing of acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not use reimbursement funds to remove, replace or dispose of any covered communications equipment or service purchased, rented, leased, or otherwise obtained (i) on or after publication of the Report and Order; or (ii) in the case of any covered communications equipment that only became covered pursuant to the Designation Orders, June 30, 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on funding use — prohibition on using funds to obtain covered equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not purchase, rent, lease, or otherwise obtain any covered communications equipment or service, using reimbursement funds or any other funds (including funds derived from private sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal requirements — permanent destruction and documentation retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must dispose of covered communications equipment or service in a manner to prevent the equipment or service from being used in the networks of other providers; the disposal must result in destruction making the equipment inoperable permanently. Recipients must retain documentation demonstrating compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status updates every 90 days until final certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must file a status update 90 days after approval of the reimbursement application and every 90 days thereafter until the final certification is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status update contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Status updates must include: (i) efforts undertaken and challenges encountered in permanently removing/replacing/disposing; (ii) availability of replacement equipment in marketplace; (iii) whether recipient has fully complied with (or is in process of complying with) all Reimbursement Program requirements; (iv) whether recipient has fully complied with (or is in process of complying with) commitments made in application; (v) whether recipient has permanently removed, replaced, and disposed of (or is in process of) all covered equipment/services that were in recipient's network as of application submission; and (vi) whether recipient has fully complied with (or is in process of complying with) the timeline submitted as required by paragraph (c)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of status updates (not earlier than 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Wireline Competition Bureau will publicly post status update filings on the Commission's website no earlier than 30 days after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report to Congress within 180 days after funding allocation stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days of completing the funding allocation stage, the Wireline Competition Bureau shall prepare a report for Congress updating on implementation efforts and recipients' work to permanently remove, replace, and dispose of covered equipment and service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spending reports (biannual filing windows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after the end of January and July, recipients must file reports with the Commission regarding how reimbursement funds have been spent, including detailed accounting of covered equipment/service permanently removed and disposed of, and the replacement equipment or service purchased, rented, leased, or otherwise obtained using reimbursement funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies starting with initial receipt of disbursement and terminates once the recipient has filed a final spending report/certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final spending report after final certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Following filing of the final certification certifying completion, the recipient must file a final spending report showing expenditure of all funds received as compared to estimated costs identified in its application for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Wireline Competition Bureau will make versions of spending reports available on its website subject to confidentiality concerns consistent with Commission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final certification within 10 days of term expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days following the expiration of the removal, replacement, and disposal term, a recipient shall file a final certification indicating whether the recipient has fully complied with (or is in the process of complying with) all terms and conditions of the Program, the commitments made in the application, the timeline submitted, and whether the recipient has permanently removed, replaced, and disposed of (or is in process of) all covered equipment or services that were in the network as of the application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient certifies it has not fully complied, it must file an updated certification when it has fully complied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation retention requirement (10 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to retain all relevant documents, including invoices and receipts, pertaining to all costs eligible for reimbursement actually incurred for removal, replacement, and disposal for a period ending not less than 10 years after the date on which it receives final disbursement from the Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audits, reviews, and field investigations — cooperation and premises access
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients shall be subject to audits and other investigations to evaluate compliance; recipients must provide consent for vendors/contractors to release confidential information to auditors/reviewers/representatives and shall permit any representative (including any auditor) appointed by the Commission to enter their premises to conduct compliance inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority to Wireline Competition Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission delegates authority to the Wireline Competition Bureau to adopt necessary policies and procedures relating to allocations, draw downs, payments, obligations, and expenditures of money from the Program to protect against waste, fraud, and abuse and, in the event of bankruptcy, to establish a Catalog of Expenses Eligible for Reimbursement and predetermined cost estimates, review estimated cost forms, issue funding allocations for costs reasonably incurred, set filing deadlines and review information and documentation regarding progress reports, allocations, and final accountings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Provider of Advanced Communications Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as a person who provides advanced communications service to United States customers; includes accredited public or private non-commercial educational institutions providing their own facilities-based educational broadband service and health care providers and libraries providing advanced communications service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement — penalties for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient violates the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act, the Commission's implementing rules, or commitments made in the application, the recipient: (1) shall repay all reimbursement funds provided; (2) shall be barred from further participation in the Program; (3) shall be referred to appropriate law enforcement agencies for further action; and (4) may be barred from participation in other Commission programs including universal service support programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to cure (180 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The penalties in paragraph (a) shall not apply unless the Commission, WCB, or Enforcement Bureau provides the recipient with notice of the violation and the recipient fails to cure the violation within 180 days after such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery of funds — immediate action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will immediately take action to recover all reimbursement funds awarded to a recipient in any case where the recipient is required to repay reimbursement funds under paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement List development — content and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall develop a list of categories of suggested replacements of physical and virtual communications equipment, application and management software, and services for the covered equipment or services on the Covered List; the list shall include categories that allow carriers the flexibility to select equipment or services that fit their needs from categories of equipment and services and the Commission may review other federal partners' efforts to inform the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Wireline Competition Bureau shall publish the Replacement List on the Commission's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement List maintenance and public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Wireline Competition Bureau shall issue a Public Notice announcing any updates to the Replacement List. If there are no updates in a calendar year, the Bureau shall issue a Public Notice announcing that no updates have been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement List neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Replacement List must be technology neutral and may not advantage the use of reimbursement funds for capital expenditures over operational expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting on covered communications equipment or services — contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each provider of advanced communications service must submit an annual report that: (1) identifies any covered equipment or service purchased/rented/leased/obtained on or after specified dates; (2) provides details on covered equipment/services in its network including type, location, date acquired, and any removal and replacement plans; (3) provides a detailed justification as to why the provider purchased/rented/leased/obtained the covered equipment/service; (4) provides information about whether any such equipment/service has been subsequently removed and replaced pursuant to the Commission's reimbursement program; (5) provides information about whether the provider plans to continue to obtain/use such equipment/service and why; and (6) includes a certification of accuracy by an appropriate official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting deadline and annual timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial reports due within 90 days after the Office of Economics and Analytics issues a public notice announcing the new reporting platform; thereafter filers must submit reports once per year on or before March 31st, reporting information as of December 31st of the previous year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting exception for providers with no covered equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provider certifies to the Commission that it does not have any covered equipment or service in its network, it is not required to submit an annual report after making such certification, unless the provider later purchases/rents/leases/obtains any covered equipment/service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Economics and Analytics authority to update reporting platform
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Economics and Analytics may implement technical improvements, changes to the format and type of data submitted, or other clarifications to the report and its instructions, consistent with the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — application form and designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit an application on FCC Form 603 or 608, as applicable, to the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau that details a Qualifying Transaction and (a) designates that the transaction seeks consideration under the ECIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — selection of prong and demonstration of requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must select the applicable prong (either § 1.60003 small carrier/Tribal Nation or § 1.60004 rural-focused) but not both, and demonstrate that the applicants meet each requirement under the selected prong.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — demonstration of unaffiliated parties (FCC Form 602)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate that the parties to the Qualifying Transaction are unaffiliated by providing a list of all affiliated entities for each party via filing a new FCC Form 602 or an updated Form 602 if ownership information is not current.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — certifications required in application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include certifications that: (i) applicants are not barred from ECIP under § 1.60007; (ii) the licenses included have not previously received ECIP benefits; (iii) applicants entered into the Qualifying Transaction in good faith and licensee/lessor reasonably believes assignee/lessee has resources and bona fide intent to meet obligations; (iv) the assignor/lessor either did not confer benefits to assignee/lessee or, if benefits were conferred, include a narrative describing any benefits; and (v) any lease for ECIP participation is for a minimum term of five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small carrier/Tribal Nation prong — eligibility exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A transaction is ineligible under this prong if it includes: (1) license(s) with existing shared construction obligations under § 1.950(g); (2) an application that includes an election to share construction obligations under § 1.950(g); (3) a light-touch leasing spectrum manager lease arrangement(s) of 3.5 GHz Priority Access Licenses in CBRS; or (4) an application that includes a barred party under § 1.60007.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small carrier/Tribal Nation prong — minimum spectrum threshold (50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ECIP transaction involving disaggregation, partition/disaggregation in combination, full license assignment, or a lease must include a minimum of 50% of the licensed spectrum and meet the minimum spectrum threshold at every point in the Transaction Geography (percentage calculated at any point as amount of spectrum assigned/leased (MHz) ÷ total spectrum held under the license (MHz)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small carrier/Tribal Nation prong — minimum Transaction Geography (25% or 10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: For partition, partition/disaggregation in combination, full assignment, or lease: minimum Transaction Geography of 25% of total licensed area for licenses with licensed area ≤30,000 sq miles, or minimum Transaction Geography of 10% for licenses with licensed area >30,000 sq miles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small carrier/Tribal Nation prong — lease minimum term (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lease arrangement, the minimum term of a long-term spectrum manager lease or de facto transfer lease is at least five (5) years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small carrier/Tribal Nation prong — good faith requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The ECIP transaction must have been entered into in good faith with a bona fide intent by all parties to meet the program's obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small carrier/Tribal Nation prong — limits on aggregating across licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple licenses may be included in a Qualifying Transaction, but spectrum and geography cannot be aggregated across multiple licenses to meet minimum thresholds; each license is considered separately and must independently meet the minimum spectrum and geography thresholds. Each license included must be either the subject of an assignment (full, partition and/or disaggregation) or a lease, but not both; a party may not assign part of a license and lease a different part of the same license to meet thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — eligibility exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A transaction is ineligible under the rural-focused prong if it includes: (1) license(s) with existing shared construction obligations pursuant to § 1.950(g); (2) an application that includes an election from the parties to share construction obligations under § 1.950(g); (3) a light-touch leasing spectrum manager lease arrangement(s) of 3.5 GHz Priority Access Licenses in CBRS; or (4) an application that includes a barred party under § 1.60007.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — minimum spectrum threshold (50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ECIP transaction involving disaggregation, partition/disaggregation in combination, or a lease must include a minimum of 50% of the licensed spectrum and meet the minimum spectrum threshold at every point in the Transaction Geography (calculated as amount assigned/leased (MHz) ÷ total spectrum (MHz)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — Qualifying Geography minimums (scaled thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum Qualifying Geography threshold of exclusively rural area is required based on license size: (i) 300 contiguous sq miles for licenses with area up to 30,000 sq miles; (ii) 900 contiguous sq miles for licenses 30,001–90,000 sq miles; (iii) 5,000 contiguous sq miles for licenses 90,001–500,000 sq miles; (iv) 15,000 contiguous sq miles for licenses 500,001 sq miles or more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — lease minimum term (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lease arrangement, the minimum term of a long-term spectrum manager lease or de facto transfer lease is at least five (5) years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — good faith requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The ECIP transaction must have been entered into in good faith with a bona fide intent by all parties to meet the program's obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — multiple contributing licenses and intersection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying Transactions must specify at least one area of Qualifying Geography; one or more licenses may contribute via assignment, partition/disaggregation, and/or leases provided the Qualifying Geography intersects each contributing license. Where multiple licenses with different sized licensed areas contribute, the Qualifying Geography must consist of the minimum geographic threshold applicable to the contributing license with the greatest square mileage.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — program benefits: five-year license term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties to a partition and/or disaggregation Qualifying Transaction; the lessor entering into a spectrum lease arrangement Qualifying Transaction; and the assignee in a full license assignment Qualifying Transaction shall receive a five-year license term extension on the license(s) subject to the application upon consummation of a Commission approved assignment/lease application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — program benefits: one-year construction extension
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties to certain Qualifying Transactions shall receive a one-year construction extension of both the interim and final performance requirement deadline, where applicable, on the license(s) subject to the application; where the Commission previously extended a performance requirement and that deadline has not passed, the ECIP one-year extension is in addition to the prior extension provided the prior extension is transferrable and the assignee separately justifies relief if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — substitution of alternative construction requirement (rural-focused assignees)
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee in a qualifying partition, combination partition/disaggregation transaction, or full license assignment filed under the rural-focused transaction prong shall be subject to the alternative construction requirement set forth in § 1.60006 in lieu of any applicable service-based performance requirement for the license(s) resulting from an ECIP transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Commission previously modified assignor's service-based requirement through waiver and such requirements have not been met, the assignee will receive the substituted alternative construction requirement benefit if the assignee separately requests and is granted a waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — limitation on duplicative benefits (single time per license)
rubrics_metrics.description: A license included in a Commission approved Qualifying Transaction shall be eligible for program benefits a single time per license for the license term and all subsequent renewal terms. A license previously included in an approved ECIP Qualifying Transaction shall be ineligible to receive benefits in any subsequent ECIP transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — obligation to comply with selected prong requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee or lessee must comply with the requirements of either the small carrier/Tribal Nation prong (§ 1.60003) or the rural-focused prong (§ 1.60004) as selected in its ECIP application and is not permitted to change prongs after consummation of the Commission-approved application/lease acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — construction requirement (100% of Qualifying Geography)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees must construct and operate, or provide signal coverage and offer service to, 100% of the Qualifying Geography identified in the Commission-approved Qualifying Transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction period is the applicable construction deadline on the license(s), as extended by § 1.60005; if no deadline remains, assignee must construct and operate/provide coverage and service to 100% of Qualifying Geography no later than two (2) years after consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — interim/final benchmark replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the assignee is subject to both an interim and final performance benchmark, the construction requirements in § 1.60006(b) replace the interim benchmark and the assignee shall not be subject to a final performance requirement. Where the assignee has only a remaining final performance requirement, the requirements in § 1.60006(b) replace the final benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — end-user device capability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All end user devices throughout the Qualifying Geography must be capable of operation on all spectrum bands associated with license(s) that contribute to the Qualifying Geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — notification of completion of construction (FCC Form 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of completion of construction must be provided to the Commission through FCC Form 601 no later than 15 days after the applicable construction deadline or expiration of the two-year period if that applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — operational requirement (100% coverage for 3 consecutive years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees must construct and operate in, or provide signal coverage and offer service to, 100% of the Qualifying Geography for at least three (3) consecutive years; operation must not fall below that used to meet the construction requirement for the entire three-year period; and assignees must meet these by the applicable construction deadline, or if none remains, the three-year period must commence no later than two (2) years after consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — lessee construction and operational requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessees must construct and operate, or provide signal coverage and offer service to, 100% of the Qualifying Geography identified in the underlying Qualifying Transaction no later than two (2) years after grant/acceptance, and must maintain operation for at least three (3) consecutive years during any period within the initial minimum five (5) year lease term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural-focused prong — operational requirement notifications (initial and final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees/lessees must file: (1) Initial operational notification within 30 days of commencement of operations providing the date operations began, certifying 100% coverage, and providing technical data demonstrating compliance; and (2) Final operational notification within 30 days of completion of the three-year operational requirement certifying 100% coverage for three consecutive years, providing the completion date, and technical data demonstrating the coverage provided during the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP — holding period for assignees (five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee of license(s) granted in a Qualifying Transaction involving a partition and/or disaggregation or full assignment is required to hold any such license(s) for a period of at least five (5) years, commencing upon the consummation date of the Commission-approved application filed pursuant to § 1.60002.
